mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly examine Team B's RECENT_5 shots (17.6) versus ALL_PRIOR shots (11.673) alongside RECENT_5 shots_on_target (5.4) versus ALL_PRIOR shots_on_target (4.02). The mechanism tests whether the within-team ratio of shots_on_target to shots shifts when shot volume is in a high-surge regime (RECENT_5 substantially above ALL_PRIOR), and whether this ratio shift is directionally consistent across historical instances of similar surge magnitude.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shot volume is elevated well above its long-run mean, the shots_on_target-to-shots ratio tends to compress (i.e., the marginal shots added in high-volume regimes are less likely to be on target), so shots_on_target rises less than proportionally with shots.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent shot volume surge (RECENT_5) relative to its long-run average is jointly associated with a divergence in shot-to-shots-on-target conversion efficiency: when a team's recent shots rise sharply but recent shots-on-target rise proportionally less, the ratio of on-target to total shots compresses, suggesting a qualitative change in shot quality or positioning that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) and their ratio across two time windows simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; the mechanism is about the joint non-linear relationship between volume and quality across windows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's RECENT_5 shots (17.6) and shots_on_target (5.4) are both above their ALL_PRIOR means (11.673 and 4.02 respectively), while RECENT_5 goals (0.8) are below the ALL_PRIOR mean (1.235). Test whether this three-way dissociation — high shots, high on-target, low goals — is a historically identifiable regime with a distinct goals-against profile for the opponent.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team enters a match in a regime of elevated shot volume and on-target shots but suppressed goals relative to long-run averages, its goals-for in that match tends to remain suppressed relative to what shot volume alone would predict, indicating a conversion-rate depression that persists across the regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent goals-for (RECENT_5) has declined relative to its long-run average despite a concurrent surge in shots and shots_on_target, suggesting a joint dissociation between shot-volume production and goal conversion that is structurally different from either observable's baseline trend alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires three observables jointly (goals, shots, shots_on_target) and a cross-window comparison (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) for each. Not reducible to any single observable or single conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A's home corner_kicks-for being substantially above its away rate, and (b) Team B's RECENT_5 corner_kicks-against being substantially below its ALL_PRIOR rate. The mechanism tests whether, in historical matches where both conditions hold simultaneously — the home team is a strong home corner producer AND the away team is in a recent low-corners-conceded regime — the realized corner total is suppressed relative to what Team A's home production rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team's elevated home corner production meets an away team in a recent low-corners-conceded regime, the realized corner count for the home team is suppressed relative to the home team's home-venue baseline, indicating the away team's recent defensive corner suppression partially offsets the home venue advantage.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetric venue split in Team A's corner_kicks-for (HOME: 6.388 vs AWAY: 4.122) combined with Team B's asymmetric corner_kicks-against (ALL_PRIOR: 5.357, RECENT_5: 3.4) creates a joint cross-team, cross-observable condition: the home team's corner production advantage interacts with the away team's recent suppression of corners conceded, and this joint state is distinct from either team's single-observable venue or recent-form split.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a two-team, two-dimension joint condition: it simultaneously uses Team A's venue split and Team B's recent-form window for the same observable. The engine covers each split individually but not their joint interaction across teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's RECENT_5 offsides-for being substantially above its ALL_PRIOR and venue-split baselines, AND Team B's RECENT_5 offsides-against being substantially below its ALL_PRIOR baseline. Test whether this joint divergence — attacker increasingly caught offside while the opponent's defensive line is increasingly disciplined — is associated with a suppression of Team A's attacking output (shots, goals) relative to its own baselines.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's recent offsides-for is elevated above its long-run mean while the defending team's recent offsides-against is depressed below its long-run mean, the attacking team's goals-for and shots-on-target tend to be suppressed relative to their own baselines, reflecting a structural mismatch in attacking line discipline versus defensive line management.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides-for has surged in RECENT_5 (3.0) relative to its ALL_PRIOR mean (1.792) and its home/away splits (HOME: 1.898, AWAY: 1.681), while Team B's offsides-against has declined in RECENT_5 (1.2) relative to its ALL_PRIOR mean (2.118). The joint state — one team's offside-trap exposure rising while the opponent's ability to trigger offsides against them is falling — represents a cross-team asymmetric divergence across two distinct observables (Team A offsides-for, Team B offsides-against) that cannot be captured by either team's single-observable recent-vs-prior comparison.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly tracking two teams' offsides observables (FOR for Team A, AGAINST for Team B) across two time windows each, and then linking this joint state to a third observable (goals/shots). Not reducible to a single observable or single conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly examine Team B's cards_2h-for (second-half, ALL_PRIOR) against its fouls-for (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) and yellow_cards-for (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR). The mechanism tests whether, in historical matches where a team's foul rate is in a low-recent regime but its second-half card rate remains at or above its long-run mean, the cards_2h outcome is better predicted by the cards_2h baseline than by the foul-rate baseline — i.e., the two observables decouple in this regime.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent foul rate drops sharply below its long-run mean but its second-half card rate remains near its long-run mean, the second-half cards outcome is not suppressed proportionally with fouls, indicating that cards_2h and fouls are not linearly coupled and that the cards_2h baseline retains predictive structure independent of the foul-rate regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: 1.367) are elevated relative to Team A's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: 1.194) and the competition context (cards_2h NEUTRAL: 1.186), while Team B's fouls-for have dropped sharply in RECENT_5 (7.4) versus ALL_PRIOR (10.633). This joint state — historically higher second-half card rate combined with a recent sharp drop in foul rate — tests whether the second-half card rate is structurally decoupled from the foul rate for Team B, i.e., whether cards_2h is driven by a different mechanism (e.g., concentration of high-severity fouls) rather than foul volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (cards_2h and fouls) across two time windows for the same team, and testing for decoupling between them. This is a non-linear / threshold relationship between two observables, not a single observable with one conditioning band.
